entry.englishMeaning: openly and at the beginning, before an agreement or activity
entry.coreIdea: Explain something openly before others commit or start.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract time-and-openness expression: disclose information clearly at the beginning, before others commit or plan.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Positive here: early disclosure is presented as helpful transparency.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Polite and practical here: “Please explain” asks for limitations early enough to plan around them.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common conversational and workplace English. “At the outset” is more formal; this is not the advance-payment sense.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Please explain any limitations up front so that we can plan around them.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: openly and at the beginning, before an agreement or activity
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker asks for limitations to be disclosed at the beginning so they can be included in planning.

when_to_use: Ask for early, clear disclosure of requirements, limits or expectations.
when_not_to_use: For information revealed only after the decision, use later or afterwards; up front would falsely imply early disclosure.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: explain / state / disclose + something + up front; be clear up front about + issue

examples.example_1: Please explain any limitations up front so that we can plan around them.
examples.example_2: I told the organiser up front that I could stay for only an hour.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: When should I mention the restricted opening hours?
B: Explain them up front, before people book.
A: I will put them in the invitation.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Using up front for a restriction disclosed only after somebody has committed.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say: The restriction should have been explained up front, but we only heard about it later.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Up front combines early timing with openness in this context; eventually merely says information became available later.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Put the important limitation on the first page before anyone signs.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: Tell me up front if the deadline is unrealistic.
memory_practice.recall_question: Why does up front matter when someone is about to make a commitment?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Explain the limit before registration. B: Reveal it after the event begins. Which discloses it up front?
memory_practice.production_task: Write two sentences explaining a project limitation up front, before your colleague agrees to the plan.

advanced_nuance: Up front here concerns early disclosure, not physical position or advance payment. The surrounding verb, such as explain or tell, makes that meaning clear.

entry.tamilMeaning: கவனிக்கவோ செயல்படவோ தூண்டும் குறிப்பு அல்லது அறிகுறி
entry.englishMeaning: a signal, sign, or prompt indicating that something should happen or be noticed
entry.coreIdea: A signal tells you to notice something or respond.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract noun for a signal that prompts an action or helps someone notice something.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral: a cue supplies a prompt without determining whether the response is good or bad.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Direct and inquisitive here: the question asks the reader to identify signals, but does not itself specify their emotional significance.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral and common in learning, communication and performance contexts. Name the situation when “cues” alone would be unclear.

meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: a signal, sign, or prompt indicating that something should happen or be noticed
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The question asks which signals the reader recognises. The short quotation does not identify those signals or their precise situation.

when_to_use: Describe a verbal, visual or other signal that prompts a response or alerts someone to a change.
when_not_to_use: Do not call an explicit detailed instruction merely a cue if its full content matters; a cue is often a brief signal or prompt.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: a cue to + action; take a cue from + person or signal; a cue for + response

examples.example_1: Her nod was my cue to begin the presentation.
examples.example_2: A flashing light gives the performers a visual cue when the music is about to start.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: How will I know when to start?
B: I will raise my hand; that is your cue.
A: I will watch for it.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: Her nod was my queue to begin.
mistakes_differences.correction: Use cue for a signal: Her nod was my cue to begin. Queue names a waiting line or sequence.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: A cue prompts a response; a clue helps solve a question or mystery. A detail can serve either purpose depending on how it is used.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A raised hand signals that it is your turn to speak.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The director's nod was my cue to start.
memory_practice.recall_question: What response does the cue prompt in your example?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: A light signals a performer to enter. B: A fingerprint helps solve a mystery. Which is primarily a cue rather than a clue?
memory_practice.production_task: Agree on a simple cue with a presentation partner and explain what action it will signal.

advanced_nuance: A cue need not be deliberately given: a long pause can be a cue to ask whether someone has a question. Interpretation still depends on the situation, so a cue is not always an unambiguous instruction.

entry.englishMeaning: calm control of emotions and behaviour under pressure
entry.coreIdea: Keep outward calm when a situation is difficult.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract noun for keeping calm and controlling reactions under pressure.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Positive: it values emotional steadiness without implying that the person feels no emotion.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Admiring and curious here: the authors ask how Greta maintained calm while “under fire.”
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral to formal; common in descriptions of difficult interactions. “Stay calm” is the everyday verbal equivalent.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: START  WITH  HEART  33  Later  that  day  we  asked  Greta  how  she had  been  able  to  keep  her  composure  under  fi re.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: calm control of emotions and behaviour under pressure
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The authors ask how Greta stayed calm and controlled her reactions while facing criticism or pressure.

when_to_use: Describe controlled, calm behaviour during criticism, embarrassment or another stressful event.
when_not_to_use: Do not assume composure means a person feels no fear or anger; the word concerns their controlled response.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: keep / maintain / regain / lose + your composure

examples.example_1: She paused to regain her composure before answering the accusation.
examples.example_2: The host kept his composure when the microphone stopped working.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: How did you answer without raising your voice?
B: I took a breath to regain my composure first.
A: That gave you time to think.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: She regained a composure after the interruption.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say: She regained her composure. Composure is normally uncountable in this sense.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Composure is controlled calm under pressure; indifference means not caring. A person can care deeply while maintaining composure.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Pause, breathe and answer steadily during a tense exchange.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: He kept his composure despite the repeated interruptions.
memory_practice.recall_question: Can someone maintain composure while feeling angry inside?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Calmly answering a difficult question despite feeling nervous. B: Not caring about the question. Which better demonstrates composure?
memory_practice.production_task: Describe a fictional speaker who regains their composure after an interruption. Show one observable action.

advanced_nuance: Regain composure implies a temporary loss of steadiness; maintain composure means preserving it. Neither phrase proves that the person feels relaxed internally.

entry.englishMeaning: according to a consistent method or recurring pattern
entry.coreIdea: Happen according to a consistent pattern rather than isolated chance.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Adverb describing a consistent pattern; here, unfair outcomes recur for particular groups rather than appearing only as isolated accidents.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral by itself; “unfair outcomes” makes the described pattern undesirable.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Analytical here: the sentence uses recurring unfairness to explain what it means for a model to be biased.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common in research and professional explanations. It does not necessarily mean someone deliberately planned the unfairness.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: A model is biased if it produces systematically unfair outcomes for certain groups.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: according to a consistent method or recurring pattern
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The sentence describes unfair outcomes recurring for certain groups in a consistent pattern. It does not say that someone deliberately planned the unfairness.

when_to_use: Describe a repeated, consistent pattern in outcomes rather than an isolated result.
when_not_to_use: A single isolated error is not enough to establish that outcomes are systematically unfair.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: systematically + verb / adjective; systematically different / excluded / unfair

examples.example_1: The selection rule systematically excluded people whose records lacked a postal address.
examples.example_2: The old timetable systematically favoured early arrivals over people using the later bus.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Is this just one unusual result?
B: No. The same rule systematically disadvantages this group.
A: Then we need to examine the pattern, not only this case.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Treating systematically as proof that someone intentionally designed an unfair result.
mistakes_differences.correction: Systematically identifies a consistent pattern; evidence of intention must be established separately.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Systematically describes a patterned or methodical process; accidentally describes lack of intention. A recurring pattern can still arise without deliberate intent.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: The same filter repeatedly leaves out the same kind of record.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The rule systematically excluded applications with incomplete addresses.
memory_practice.recall_question: Does systematically unfair necessarily mean deliberately unfair?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: The same rule repeatedly disadvantages one group. B: One unrelated clerical mistake. Which supports the description systematically unfair?
memory_practice.production_task: Describe an invented procedure that systematically leaves out one type of application. Explain the recurring rule without assuming anyone's motive.

advanced_nuance: Systematically can describe deliberate method, as in checking files systematically, or a consistent outcome pattern, as in the source. Here the pattern is the focus; the adverb alone does not establish intention.

entry.englishMeaning: an updated schedule showing when planned work will happen
entry.coreIdea: An existing schedule has been changed.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract scheduling phrase: an existing timetable has been changed to reflect a new plan.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral: a revision may be an improvement or a response to difficulty; the phrase alone does not imply failure.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Factual here: the sentence identifies an additional week for testing without blaming anyone.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common in workplace planning. “Updated schedule” is an equally natural, slightly plainer alternative.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: The revised timeline includes an extra week for testing.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: an updated schedule showing when planned work will happen
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The updated schedule now allows an additional week for testing.

when_to_use: Refer to a schedule changed after an earlier version was circulated or agreed.
when_not_to_use: For the first proposed schedule, use initial or proposed timeline rather than revised timeline.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: the revised timeline for + project; issue / share / follow + a revised timeline

examples.example_1: The revised timeline includes an extra week for testing.
examples.example_2: Please use the revised timeline when booking volunteers for the exhibition.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Is the launch still planned for Monday?
B: No. The revised timeline moves it to Thursday.
A: I will update the invitation.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Calling the first-ever project schedule the revised timeline.
mistakes_differences.correction: Use revised timeline when an earlier schedule has changed; use initial timeline for the first version.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: A revised timeline changes the schedule; a progress report describes how work is going and may leave the schedule unchanged.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: An old date is crossed out and a new date is added.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The revised timeline gives us another week for testing.
memory_practice.recall_question: What previous document or agreement is implied by revised timeline?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: The first schedule is created. B: An existing schedule is updated after a delay. Which produces a revised timeline?
memory_practice.production_task: Announce a revised timeline for a small project. State one changed date and the reason for the change.

advanced_nuance: A revised timeline need not be longer than the original; dates can move earlier or tasks can be reordered. State the actual changes rather than assuming that revised means delayed.

entry.tamilMeaning: ஒருவர்மீது சுமத்தப்படும் கடினமான பொறுப்பு, கடமை அல்லது பிரச்சினை
entry.englishMeaning: a difficult responsibility, duty, or problem placed on someone
entry.coreIdea: A responsibility feels like a heavy load.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Figurative noun for a difficult responsibility, drawing on the idea of a heavy load someone must carry.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Negative in this sense: it emphasizes the effort or pressure a responsibility places on a person.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Reassuring or defensive here: “I'm not trying” denies an intention to place that pressure on the listener.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common in both everyday and professional English. “Responsibility” is more neutral when the hardship is not the point.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: I'm  not  trying  to  put  the  burden  on  you.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: a difficult responsibility, duty, or problem placed on someone
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker denies intending to place a difficult responsibility or pressure on the listener.

when_to_use: Emphasise the strain caused by a duty, responsibility or problem.
when_not_to_use: For a neutral allocation of ordinary work, responsibility or task may avoid the negative weight carried by burden.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: put / place a burden on + person; bear / share / ease the burden

examples.example_1: Managing every booking alone put a heavy burden on the organiser.
examples.example_2: The neighbours shared the burden of maintaining the community garden.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: I cannot organise the whole event by myself.
B: You should not have to bear that burden alone.
A: Let us divide the jobs among the group.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: The extra work put a burden to her.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say: The extra work put a burden on her. Use on for the person carrying the responsibility.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Responsibility identifies a duty; burden highlights its difficulty, pressure or cost to the person carrying it.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A heavy backpack represents too many responsibilities.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: Sharing the work eased the burden on the team leader.
memory_practice.recall_question: What extra feeling does burden add compared with responsibility?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: A difficult duty overwhelming one person. B: A small optional activity they enjoy. Which is more naturally called a burden?
memory_practice.production_task: Ask a team to share a difficult responsibility. Use burden without blaming the person currently doing the work.

advanced_nuance: Calling a person a burden can sound deeply hurtful because it frames the person as a load. In this lesson the burden is the responsibility or problem; name it clearly when discussing workload.

entry.word: how does that work in practice
entry.englishMeaning: used to ask how an idea is carried out in real situations
entry.coreIdea: Ask how a proposal operates in a real situation.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Conversational question about implementation: ask how an idea functions in a real situation rather than only in theory.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral: it can request useful detail without rejecting the idea.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Practical and probing here: the manager's absence is offered as a specific situation to explain.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Natural in professional and everyday discussions. The full question is clearer than an unexplained challenge such as “Really?”

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: How does that work in practice when the manager is away?
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: used to ask how an idea is carried out in real situations
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker asks how the arrangement functions when the manager is absent, making the question concrete.

when_to_use: Request steps, responsibilities or a realistic example after hearing a general proposal.
when_not_to_use: Do not use a dismissive tone if you simply want clarification; follow the question with the situation you need explained.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: How does that work in practice + when / if + situation?
common_collocations: how does that work in practice when someone is absent
how does that work in practice for a small team

examples.example_1: How does that work in practice when the manager is away?
examples.example_2: How does that work in practice for a family sharing one car?

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Any team member can approve a booking.
B: How does that work in practice if two people approve it at once?
A: The first approval locks the record.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: How that works in practice when someone is absent?
mistakes_differences.correction: Ask: How does that work in practice when someone is absent? Use does before the subject and the base verb work.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: How does that work in practice asks about implementation; why is that necessary asks for the reason behind the proposal.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Turn a diagram into the steps someone follows on a busy day.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: How does that work in practice when two people need help at once?
memory_practice.recall_question: Are you asking for the purpose of the idea or its actual operation?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Ask who takes each step during a real incident. B: Ask who first invented the idea. Which answers how it works in practice?
memory_practice.production_task: Respond to a proposal for shared equipment with how does that work in practice and add one realistic situation involving conflicting needs.

advanced_nuance: How does that work in practice can be curious or challenging depending on tone. A specific scenario helps make it a constructive request for detail instead of a vague expression of doubt.

entry.englishMeaning: visual interfaces that summarize and monitor important measurements
entry.coreIdea: Screens bring important measurements together for monitoring.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Technical noun for visual displays that bring important measurements together for monitoring; the computing use extends the vehicle-instrument image.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral: a dashboard can support monitoring but does not guarantee that problems will be detected.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Explanatory here: the sentence lists dashboards and automated alerts as ways some teams monitor drift.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Standard workplace and software vocabulary. “A screen showing key measurements” is a useful explanation for new users.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Some teams build dashboards or set up an automated alert to catch drift early.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: visual interfaces that summarize and monitor important measurements
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The source names dashboards as one way teams monitor model drift, alongside automated alerts.

when_to_use: Describe visual interfaces that gather key measurements or status information in one place.
when_not_to_use: A dashboard is not automatically an alerting system; somebody may need to look at it to notice a change.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: build / view / monitor + dashboards; dashboards showing + measurements

examples.example_1: The operations team checks its dashboards for changes in response time.
examples.example_2: The school uses dashboards to summarise attendance across its classes.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Where can I see the weekly totals?
B: They are on the reporting dashboards.
A: Do those update every day or only at the end of the week?

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Assuming dashboards automatically notify users whenever a number changes.
mistakes_differences.correction: Dashboards display information; check whether separate alerts are configured if notification is needed.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Dashboards present measurements visually; alerts actively draw attention to a condition. One system can provide both.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Several important gauges appear together on one screen.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: Our dashboards show response times and recent errors together.
memory_practice.recall_question: What is the difference between viewing dashboards and receiving alerts?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: A screen summarising several key measures. B: A single notification that a limit was crossed. Which is a dashboard?
memory_practice.production_task: Describe two measurements you would include on dashboards for a small online service, and explain who would use them.

advanced_nuance: Dashboards summarise selected measurements, so their apparent completeness depends on what was chosen and when the data was refreshed. A clear dashboard can still omit an important problem.

entry.tamilMeaning: ஒரு பிரச்சினையையோ மோதலையோ மீண்டும் திடீரெனக் கடுமையாக அணுகுதல்
entry.englishMeaning: to return suddenly and aggressively to an issue or confrontation
entry.coreIdea: Return to a disagreement with sudden force.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Figurative description of returning forcefully to a confrontation, like rushing back into a physical charge.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Negative or cautionary here: it suggests an aggressive return rather than a calm resumption.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Challenging and self-reflective here: the question asks readers to notice a pattern of withdrawal followed by forceful confrontation.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Vivid conversational or narrative wording. “Return to the discussion aggressively” is more explicit in a behaviour report.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Do  you  walk  away  from  some  issues  only  to  come  charging  back  into  other s?
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: to return suddenly and aggressively to an issue or confrontation
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The question asks whether the reader withdraws from some issues but returns forcefully to others. Charging makes the return sound aggressive rather than calm.

when_to_use: Describe someone re-entering a dispute or discussion abruptly and forcefully.
when_not_to_use: For a calm return to an unfinished topic, use come back to the issue or resume the discussion.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: come charging back into + discussion; come charging back with + accusation
common_collocations: come charging back into the argument
come charging back with another accusation

examples.example_1: He left the discussion, only to come charging back with another accusation.
examples.example_2: Please do not come charging back into the argument before everyone has calmed down.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: I need a break from this discussion.
B: Take one, but let us return calmly rather than come charging back with more accusations.
A: Agreed. We can talk again after lunch.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Using come charging back to describe an entirely calm, measured return without intending a contrast.
mistakes_differences.correction: Use come charging back for a forceful return; say resume the discussion for a neutral return.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Come back describes returning; come charging back adds speed, force and, in this confrontation sense, aggression.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Someone returns to the room already launching another accusation.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: He was ready to come charging back into the debate.
memory_practice.recall_question: What attitude does charging add to come back here?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Return quietly and ask to clarify one point. B: Return abruptly with angry accusations. Which better fits come charging back?
memory_practice.production_task: Describe a fictional disagreement in which someone is tempted to come charging back, then chooses a calmer response.

advanced_nuance: Come charging back borrows the force of a physical charge to describe conversational behaviour. The person need not literally run; it is the abrupt, aggressive return that matters in this sense.

entry.englishMeaning: a problem that delays or reverses progress
entry.coreIdea: A difficulty pushes progress backwards or delays it.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract noun for a problem that interrupts, delays or reverses progress.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Negative but often limited: it names a difficulty without necessarily implying total failure.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Resilient and matter-of-fact here: losing the venue is acknowledged, then balanced by finding another hall.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral and common in everyday and workplace English. Its severity depends on the situation; it is not automatically a minor problem.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Losing the venue was a setback, but we found another hall.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: a problem that delays or reverses progress
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: Losing the venue disrupted the plan, but the organisers recovered by finding another hall.

when_to_use: Describe a problem that interrupts progress toward a goal.
when_not_to_use: Do not automatically treat a setback as the final failure of the whole effort; the work may continue or recover.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: suffer / face / overcome + a setback; a setback for + plan

examples.example_1: Losing the venue was a setback, but we found another hall.
examples.example_2: A broken sewing machine caused a setback in her plans for the exhibition.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: The first venue is no longer available.
B: That is a setback, but we still have two alternatives.
A: I will contact them today.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Assuming a setback means the project has permanently failed.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say: We faced a setback and need to revise the plan. Reserve failed for an outcome that actually warrants it.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: A setback hinders progress; a failure names an unsuccessful outcome. A setback may contribute to failure, but does not necessarily lead to it.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A marker moves backwards on a progress chart, then starts forward again.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The delay was a setback, but it did not end the project.
memory_practice.recall_question: Can a project succeed after suffering a setback?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: A delay requires a new schedule but work continues. B: The goal is achieved on time. Which is a setback?
memory_practice.production_task: Describe a setback in a fictional community event and one practical action that helps the team recover.

advanced_nuance: Setback does not mean minor. Major setback and serious setback are natural combinations; the surrounding description establishes severity and prospects of recovery.
